reasons: No loopback CDP listener before the spike: ss -ltn showed no 9222/9223/9229; curl http://127.0.0.1:{9222,9223,9229}/json/version all failed.
The chrome-devtools MCP browser runs with --remote-debugging-pipe (not a TCP port), which list-browser-targets cannot consume, and it held only about:blank.
The user's main Chrome process tree has no --remote-debugging-port.
REA CDP surfaces are attach-only and never launch a browser, so they cannot create the missing target.

baselineComparison.residualNonRedundantProperty: REA's passive capture retains a content-addressed, privacy-filtered structural snapshot (tag names, attribute NAMES, accessibility roles, node counts, href URLs) that needs no page JS injection. This is complementary in principle to a drift tripwire, but on the tested case it recovered strictly less than the existing Playwright path, so no incremental value is demonstrated.

sensitiveMaterialHandling: All observed page content was synthetic placeholder text authored for this spike. No member names, post bodies, URNs, profile slugs, cookies, tokens or localStorage values from any real LinkedIn session were captured, exported or committed. REA's own capture defaults (values redacted, storage keys off, accessibility text off) were left at their conservative defaults.
noCodeChangeRationale: This repo already asserts the promoted/featured label envelope (tests/unit/pattern-data.test.js:199-226, including rejecting 'Featured by the CEO'), already exercises the promoted toggle on the legacy container shape (tests/extension-interactions.js:1404-1470) and already pins modern-shape fail-open behaviour for manual controls (tests/extension-interactions.js:3113-3150). Adding fixtures for label variants would duplicate existing assertions, and the pilot produced no directly observed LinkedIn false negative to justify new coverage.
